methods.label: Track the carries
methods.explanation:
The repeated eights make the multiplication predictable: after the first two columns, the same carry repeats. Let \(R=8(1+10+\cdots+10^{k-1})\), the number with \(k\) eights.

If \(k=1\), then \(8R=64\), whose digit sum is only \(10\). Now suppose \(k\ge2\). In multiplying \(R\) by \(8\), the units column gives \(8\cdot8=64\), so we write \(4\) and carry \(6\). The next column gives \(64+6=70\), so we write \(0\) and carry \(7\). Every remaining column gives \(64+7=71\), so we write \(1\) and keep carrying \(7\). The final carry becomes the leading digit.

Thus the product has a leading \(7\), then \(k-2\) ones, and finally \(04\). Its digit sum is
\[
7+(k-2)+0+4=k+9.
\]
Therefore \(k+9=1000\), giving \(\boxed{k=991}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
